headline: Netanyahu 'campaigning to resume strikes', instructed IDF to plan new offensive
dek: New details beyond the 1700-08/1700-10 contested baseline: (1) FT sources say Netanyahu is 'currently campaigning to resume large-scale strikes against Iran, and recently instructed the IDF to plan for a new offensive'; (2) Israeli officials shared an UPDATED target list with US counterparts…
sources: Financial Times (3 unnamed sources); relayed via JPost article-912360 (Oct 21 08:02 IDT), Haaretz (Oct 21 08:33 IDT), Yonhap/en.nocutnews, Azernews, albawaba, matzav
fault_line: Is Trump restraining a reckless pre-election war, or just timing it for after the ballots are counted — and is Netanyahu campaigning on war or actually planning one?

sections.what_happened: New details beyond the 1700-08/1700-10 contested baseline: (1) FT sources say Netanyahu is 'currently campaigning to resume large-scale strikes against Iran, and recently instructed the IDF to plan for a new offensive'; (2) Israeli officials shared an UPDATED target list with US counterparts including civilian infrastructure not hit in February's campaign; (3) one source: 'There will either be a deal or an attack'; a joint US-Israel operation in coming weeks is 'a realistic possibility'; (4) Haaretz relay of Fox News: Israel held a Tuesday drill sending fighter jets toward Iran through Syria/Iraq; (5) Yonhap: IDF has canceled soldiers' leave, maintains alert; (6) NEW WH statement: White House Principal Deputy Press Secretary Anna Kelly told Al Jazeera (via Sputnik/UNI India, Oct 21) 'The United States will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the midterm elections' — corroborates Trump's Oct 8 statement that the US would refrain from attacking Iran until after Nov 3. Counterpoint stands: JPost 912399 (Bob, Oct 21 12:40, IDF sources) says IDF never prepared the Oct 10 attack and the 'Trump blocked it' premise is wrong.
sections.what_verified: Trump Oct 8 ruling-out of US attack before Nov 3 (multiple outlets); Axios Oct 13 report of Netanyahu-Trump strike discussions; Iran-rebuild-of-nuclear-infrastructure concern (Axios); Fox News drill relay; Yonhap leave-cancellation.
sections.what_disputed: JPost 912399: IDF sources deny any Oct-10 attack plan existed — 'Trump could not block an attack that was not planned'; premise of election-influence leak theory (both sides could benefit).
sections.why_matters: The ballot-box clock now governs the battlefield: Trump freezes strikes until Nov 3 midterms while Netanyahu (Oct 27 vote, trailing in polls) is reported to be campaigning to resume them. Publish BOTH the FT claim and the JPost denial side-by-side — reliability supremacy demands it.
sections.context: Background: US-Iran — FT 'deal or attack' story matures: Netanyahu 'campaigning to resume strikes', instructed IDF to plan new offensive; WH official: no US attack before midterms

totw_analysis: Our read: The ballot-box clock now governs the battlefield: Trump freezes strikes until Nov 3 midterms while Netanyahu (Oct 27 vote, trailing in polls) is reported to be campaigning to resume them. Publish BOTH the FT claim and the JPost denial side-by-side — reliability supremacy demands it. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Trump restraining a reckless pre-election war, or just timing it for after the ballots are counted — and is Netanyahu campaigning on war or actually planning one?
